_about: Vendor search modes the normalized search_depth does not reach, for setups written provider:mode. Each is sent as provider_options, which a search merges last, so it overrides what web-router would send for the same field. Checked against each vendor's docs on 2026-09-30; see PRICING.md for sources. 'verified' is true only when a live call has shown the mode changing what comes back; 'observed' records what the last check saw. Linkup's standard mode was checked live; Exa, Tavily and Parallel modes are unchecked.

fast.note: Tavily's own lower-latency tier, 1 credit. Not web-router's fast, which sends advanced.

ultra-fast.note: Lowest latency, one summary per URL, 1 credit.

highlights.note: Highlights instead of the full text web-router asks for; same $1 per 1k pages.

fast.note: Lower-latency, lower-cost search, $1 per 1k against $5 for the default web.
fast.observed: 2026-09-30: sent and accepted, but the response was byte-identical to the default on the one query tried, so its effect is not yet shown.

context-low.note: Short passages per page; the default is high. No price difference.
context-low.observed: 2026-09-30: sent and accepted, but the response was byte-identical to the default on the one query tried, so its effect is not yet shown.

context-medium.note: Balanced passages per page. No price difference.
context-medium.observed: 2026-09-30: sent and accepted, but the response was byte-identical to the default on the one query tried, so its effect is not yet shown.

extra-snippets.note: Up to 5 extra excerpts per result, included in the Search plan.
extra-snippets.observed: 2026-09-30: sent and accepted, but the response was byte-identical to the default on the one query tried, so its effect is not yet shown.

full-content.note: Live-scraped full page per result; with @lite it is lite plus full content, which web-router's depths don't offer. +$1 per 1k URLs.
full-content.observed: 2026-09-30, with @lite: 590 characters of results became 285,145 and the search took 106s instead of 2.7s.

full-page-cache.note: Full pages from You.com's cache only, which it doesn't bill; web-router's deep lets it fetch live.
full-page-cache.observed: 2026-09-30: sent and accepted, but the response was byte-identical to the default on the one query tried, so its effect is not yet shown.

standard.note: Linkup's single agentic pass for queries spanning several topics, $5 per 1k like flash and fast.
standard.observed: 2026-09-30: against the default fast depth it changed which pages came back on one of three queries (33,936 characters against 34,723) and returned the same pages in the same order on the other two.

flash.note: Linkup's lowest-latency depth, $5 per 1k. Same snippet size as fast.
flash.observed: 2026-09-30: accepted; about 0.4s against 1s for fast, snippets of the same size.

deep.note: Several search iterations, 6-16s, billed $50 per 1k in Linkup's docs. Same snippet size as fast.
deep.observed: 2026-09-30: accepted; 6-16s against 1s for fast, snippets of the same size, and different pages ranked.

turbo.note: Parallel's fastest /v1 mode, $1 per 1k; English and Japanese only. Unset, web-router sends fast.

basic.note: Longer excerpts at about a second, $5 per 1k: Parallel's nearest /v1 mode to the beta's one-shot output.

advanced.note: /v1's own default and the beta's agentic tier: more retrieval and compression, about 3s, $5 per 1k.

realtime.note: Keenable's fastest search mode, billed as its own SKU (search.realtime); unset, a search runs in pro.
realtime.observed: 2026-10-13: accepted and echoed back as the mode that served the call, about 0.3s; on one query it returned the same five pages with the same content as pro.

content.note: Adds each result's page body. Unset, content is the summary. Same price per call.
content.observed: 2026-10-19: content went from empty to the page body (16,850 characters on one result); snippet and summary unchanged.
